title: Invert Binary Tree
description:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, **invert** the tree (mirror it horizontally so every node's left and right subtrees are swapped), and return its root.

If the tree is empty (`root` is `null`), return `null`.
hints: Inverting a binary tree means swapping the left and right children of every node in the tree.
Recursively invert the left and right subtrees and assign `node.left, node.right = invert(node.right), invert(node.left)`.
You can also do this iteratively using a queue (BFS) or stack (DFS), swapping each popped node's children before pushing them.

examples.explanation: Swap 2 and 7 under 4, then swap (1, 3) and (6, 9) -> [4, 7, 2, 9, 6, 3, 1].
Swapping the left child 1 and right child 3 of root 2 yields [2, 3, 1].
